description:
Block until the next inbound message arrives and return it with its thread context, so you can answer with reply.
When: the user asks you to chat, keep replying or respond to the next message.
Loop: wait → reply → wait again, passing each result's after_id. On "timeout" or "interrupted" (server restart) call again with the returned after_id; nothing is replayed or lost. Same-thread messages arriving within settle_seconds come as ONE result: reply once, to reply_target_id; next says what to do.
Skipped: your own messages, reactions and no-reply messages (listed in skipped). Messages on other threads are not returned: after_id moves past them and pending_ids lists them; read them with get_thread before waiting again.
Limits: each call blocks at most timeout_seconds (max 230). In chat hosts each wait is a model turn: tell the user you are listening and for how long, and stop when they interrupt or their limits are reached.

after_id.description: only messages with a greater id qualify; pass the after_id from the previous result. Omit on the first call to wait for messages arriving from now on

from.description: only accept messages from this address or short name

include_thread.description: include the assembled thread context of the newest message

settle_seconds.description: after the first message, keep collecting same-thread messages for this long

thread_of.description: only accept messages in this message's thread

name: wait_for_message

after_id.description: pass this as after_id on the next call

attachments.description: sorted by filename, the same order in every tool

type.description: media type; inferred from the filename when the host records none

compressed.description: true when the body was sent deflate-compressed on the wire (see size)

preview.description: start of the body; may be shorter than the full body

reaction.description: the emoji when this message is itself a reaction ("" clears one); null otherwise

read.description: null when not applicable (your own sent messages)

size.description: body size in bytes as stored by your host: for a message you received with compressed true, the compressed wire length; your own sent messages store the uncompressed length. body_bytes, where given, is the decoded length

next.description: what to do with this result

pending_ids.description: ids of pending_other_threads, oldest first: read these before waiting again

pending_other_threads.description: new messages not returned here (other threads, or beyond the batch limit); after_id has moved past them, so read each with get_thread or get_message

reply_target_id.description: newest message of the batch; reply to this one

skipped.description: messages deliberately passed over; after_id has advanced past them

emoji.description: for reactions: the emoji ("" clears a reaction)

reaction_to.description: for reactions: the message reacted to

reason.description: one of "own", "reaction", "no_reply", "from_mismatch", "other_thread". More values may be added

status.description: one of "message", "timeout", "interrupted"; interrupted: the server is restarting; call again with after_id. More values may be added

thread_topic.description: the thread root's topic (replies carry none); null when unknown

transport.description: one of "websocket", "poll". More values may be added

unclassified.description: messages whose thread could not be determined; after_id is held before them, call again to retry

title: Wait for next fmsg message
